New!
  
🚀 Improvement for a Smoother Experience
We’ve been listening! This update enhances your day-to-day on-the-go management by fixing key frustrations and by improving attachments in tasks and guest messages.
What’s New?
✅ For iOS & Android Users:
Effortless typing & messaging – The keyboard now responds instantly, so you can reply to guests, create tasks, and update information without frustrating delays.
Stay in control while typing – The app now adjusts to your screen size, keeping key information visible even when the keyboard is open—no more blind typing!
Seamless, faster navigation – We’ve optimized background processes to eliminate slowdowns, ensuring smooth, uninterrupted use.
Stronger, more reliable performance – Fewer crashes, smoother transitions, and a more stable experience let you manage bookings, tasks, and messages with ease.
🔹 For Android Users:
Easily attach photos & files – Need to send a maintenance update or clarify a guest request? You can now upload documents or snap a photo directly in task comments or inbox messages.
📌 Update now to version 1.0.1 on Android! iOS users, ensure you’re on the latest version (1.1.0) to enjoy these improvements.
Thank you for being part of the Smily community! 💙

articles.author: Basile, Product Manager
articles.description:
New!
  
We’re excited to announce our integration with a new Booking.com’s API, bringing you clearer insights into each reservation’s fees and taxes. 
Those new informations are available for all Property Managers using Payment by booking (with VCC and Bank transfer), whether you’re using partial or full sync with Booking.com.
What’s New?
Detailed price breakdown: You’ll now see clearer information on rental fees, cleaning fees, service charges, and city taxes directly in the reservation details as below; 



Withheld tax details: In regions where Booking.com withholds tax on your behalf, you’ll see exactly how much was withheld and paid to authorities.


Current balance & VCC info: More visibility on the Virtual Credit Card (VCC) balance, plus its activation and expiration dates.


    
How Does this affect you?
Depending on how Booking.com handles the city tax for each reservation, you’ll see one of these scenarios:
1- Booking.com collects and remits city tax directly to the authorities:
Your payment bar will show two payments (one for the rental and one for the withheld tax).

Since Booking.com pays the tax on your behalf, the payment bar will appear “complete.”
2- Booking.com collects the city tax from the guest and includes it in the VCC; you are responsible for remitting the tax:
The city tax is included in your total payout, so the payment bar will also appear “complete.”


Don’t forget to pay the tax to your local authorities.


3- Booking.com does not collect the city tax; you must collect and remit it yourself:
The payment bar will show the rental amount only (city tax is missing).


You must collect the city tax from guests at check-in and pay it to the authorities.


The city tax is missing from the payment bar, you should collect it before/on check-in.


-> Automatic payment link should be disabled in these cases, Booking.com does not include it in the payment because of regulations.
If you have any questions, please reach out to us 🙂
Your Smily team!
articles.title: Booking.com - Introducing clearer fee & tax breakdown for your reservations

articles.description:
Description: Potential for continued admin console access past inactivity timeout
What happened?
The admin console session timeout works by recording tailnet-specific activity timestamps on login and from browser requests triggered by user activity. Previously the admin console also erroneously considered the act of switching between multiple tailnets to be a login and recorded a fresh timestamp for the user in the destination tailnet while switching.
For tailnets whose users were also members of other tailnets with less strict inactivity timeouts, these users may have been able to continue their access to the admin console for longer than expected if they switched between tailnets and did not time out of the less restrictive tailnet.
The issue was present since inactivity timeout was initially released in August 2024, and was fixed in production on March 7th, 2025. A user who switches to a tailnet in which their session has already expired will be logged out and redirected to the login page.
Who was affected?
Tailnets with admin console session timeout configurations and users who are members of other tailnets with less strict session timeout configurations.
What was the impact?
Users of tailnets with strict admin console session timeouts may have been able to continue their access to the admin console past expected timeouts by switching to and from other tailnets in the admin console whose console configurations were less strict.
What do I need to do?
No action is required.

articles.description:
Incident began at 2025-03-10 10:50 and ended at 2025-03-10 13:30 (times are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)).

Incident Report

Summary

On Monday, March 10, 2025, at 03:50 US/Pacific, NotebookLM experienced an outage where users were unable to use chat, upload sources, or use interactive audio features globally for 2 hours and 40 minutes.

We deeply regret the disruption our Google Workspace customers experienced. We know you rely on our services, and we fell short of meeting your expectations. We are committed to improving our platform's reliability and performance, and we are taking immediate steps to improve the platform’s performance and availability.

Root Cause

The root cause has been determined to be permission errors that impeded NotebookLM's access to the necessary underlying model.

Subsequent to a recent configuration change, the model was assigned to incorrect access control lists (ACLs) by the internal router that manages the models. This change resulted in the NotebookLM model being associated with a default model family possessing more stringent access controls.

Therefore, the NotebookLM model encountered permission errors, and incoming requests were rejected, culminating in customer inability to utilize the impacted features.

Remediation and Prevention

Google engineers were alerted of the outage from our internal monitoring system on March 10, 2025, at 03:50 US/Pacific, and immediately started an investigation. Once the underlying cause was identified, Google engineers added the required access controls to the default model at 06:30 US/Pacific to fully mitigate the impact.

Google is committed to preventing a repeat of this issue in the future and is completing the following actions:

  • Implement a failsafe mechanism on the internal system that manages the Machine Learning (ML) models. This will prevent similar issues from occurring due to unintended configuration changes.

  • Updating the configuration of the router to bypass the access control check when models are moved to the internal system.

Detailed Description of Impact

Between 03:50 US/Pacific and 06:30 US/Pacific on Monday, 10 March 2025, NotebookLM and Enterprise users were unable to use chat, upload sources, or use interactive audio. Customers experienced errors up to 100% due to this incident related to permission errors.

Affected products: NotebookLM
articles.title: RESOLVED: We're investigating reports of an issue with NotebookLM. We will provide more information shortly. The affected users are unable to access NotebookLM.

Mar 12, 14:07 UTC
Resolved - On March 12, 2025, between 13:28 UTC and 14:07 UTC, the Actions service experienced degradation leading to run start delays. During the incident, about 0.6% of workflow runs failed to start, 0.8% of workflow runs were delayed by an average of one hour, and 0.1% of runs ultimately ended with an infrastructure failure. The issue stemmed from connectivity problems between the Actions services and certain nodes within one of our Redis clusters. The service began recovering once connectivity to the Redis cluster was restored at 13:41 UTC. These connectivity issues are typically not a concern because we can fail over to healthier replicas. However, due to an unrelated issue, there was a replication delay at the time of the incident, and failing over would have caused a greater impact on our customers. We are working on improving our resiliency and automation processes for this infrastructure to improve the speed of diagnosing and resolving similar issues in the future.

During this time, 34% of Actions workflow runs experienced delays, and a small percentage of runs using GitHub-hosted runners failed to start. Additionally, Pages deployments for sites without a custom Actions workflow (93% of them) did not run, preventing new changes from being deployed. 
An unexpected data shape led to crashes in some of our pods. We mitigated the incident by excluding the affected pods and correcting the data that led to the crashes. The incident was mitigated by halting execution of the problematic background job and disabling the feature flag controlling the job execution. Resolved - On February 26, 2025, between 14:51 UTC and 17:19 UTC, GitHub Packages experienced a service degradation, leading to billing-related failures when uploading and downloading Packages. During this period, the billing usage and budget pages were also inaccessible. Initially, we reported that GitHub Actions was affected, but we later determined that the impact was limited to jobs interacting with Packages services, while jobs that did not upload or download Packages remained unaffected.
The incident occurred due to an error in newly introduced code, which caused containers to get into a bad state, ultimately leading to billing API calls failing with 503 errors. We mitigated the issue by rolling back the contributing change. In response to this incident, we are enhancing error handling, improving the resiliency of our billing API calls to minimize customer impact, and improving change rollout practices to catch these potential issues prior to deployment.

articles.description: On March 14, 2025 from 2:15 PM PDT to 3:22 PM PDT, users attempting to log into the Slack Desktop client and some users signing into the web client were unable to complete sign-in, and were seeing a blank purple screen.We discovered that a recent code change relating to our sign-in process was causing an incorrect API call which resulted in the inability to log in. We rolled back this code change, fixed the code, and redeployed, resolving the issue for all affected users.
articles.title: Incident: Desktop app version 4.43.43 not loading for some users

articles.description: From around 6:45 AM PST on February 26, 2025 to 8:30 AM PST on February 27, 2025, Slack users experienced issues with our Events API. Specifically, custom applications, integrations, and bots may not have worked as expected. Additionally, some users may have experienced issues with @mentioning Slack Connect channel members.This issue was a result of the mitigation measures we took while working to resolve a concurrent incident. To help us address the initial incident, we paused the Events API job queue and rate-limited a non-critical API endpoint that was generating an outsized load. While the queue was paused, incoming Events API requests were placed in a backlog. Once we stabilized the database tier and restored critical Slack functionality, we re-enabled the Events API queue at around 11:27 PM PST on February 26, 2025. From this point onwards, all new events were processed as expected. We made the decision not to replay the backlogged events to avoid confusion over significantly delayed app responses, and to avoid a surge of queued events for both our own systems and those of third-party providers. We continued working to address lingering issues with Slack Connect @mentions, fully resolving the incident for all impacted users at 8:30 AM PST on February 27, 2025.
articles.title: Incident: Custom Applications and Bots may not be working as expected

articles.description: On March 10, 2025, from 12:47 PM PDT to 1:42 PM PDT, all users may have experienced issues with search in Slack. File, message, and channel searches did not return results, and the admin dashboard may not have loaded correctly.A misconfiguration in our search-related infrastructure caused queries to fail to resolve.To restore search behaviour, we scaled up our infrastructure and redirected incoming search requests to other servers. In parallel, we rolled back the incorrect configuration on the impacted search server. Once this was complete, we verified that the affected search server was functioning normally once again. We resumed the flow of search traffic to this server, fully resolving the issue for all users.
articles.title: Incident: Issues with Search in Slack

articles.description: From 6:45 AM PST to 4:13 PM PST on February 26, 2025, a large percentage of Slack users experienced issues with various features including sending and receiving messages, using workflows, loading channels or threads, and logging into Slack. These features may have been degraded or in some cases fully unusable.  We traced this issue to a maintenance action in one of our database systems, which, combined with a latent defect in our caching system, caused an overload of heavy traffic to the database. As a result, approximately 50% of instances relying on this database became unavailable. We took several actions to reduce the heavy load on the database system and implemented a fix for the source of the load. At around 9:32 AM PST, we observed improved health metrics for some affected Slack features and at around 4:13 PM PST, our health metrics returned to normal rates, indicating the issue was resolved for all affected users.Edit: After the main impact of this issue was resolved, users experienced issues with our Events API - specifically related to custom applications, integrations and bots not working. This issue is now resolved and these are functioning as expected. You can review specific updates on this resolution here: https://slack-status.com/2025-02/d41e4bfd1ccae26a.
articles.title: Outage: Trouble loading or using Slack

articles.description: From 7:19 PM PST on February 23, 2025 to 3:14 PM PST on February 24, 2025, some users may have been unable to use @here, @channel or @everyone mentions in the Slack for iOS app on version 25.02.30.A routine code update introduced an error in the most recent version of the Slack for iOS app, which prevented these mentions from autocompleting or sending correctly.We released a fix in version 25.02.31 (available via the Apple App Store), which resolved these issues for all impacted users.
articles.title: Incident: Specific @-mentions like @channelname, @here and @everyone are not working on iOS app version 25.02.30

articles.description: From 2:00 PM PST on February 9, 2025, to 8:24 PM PST on February 11, 2025, some users experienced issues with custom emoji failing to load. A backend process responsible for handling custom emoji was experiencing an unexpected spike of requests, resulting in a backlog. This backlog primarily caused delays with recently added emoji. We made a change to restart emoji rendering jobs to help with request traffic, resolving the issue for all affected users.
articles.title: Incident: Custom emoji not loading

articles.description: From 9:00 AM PST on February 14, 2025 to 4:30 PM PST on February 19, 2025, iOS users with Slack set to a non-English language were unable to set a default status and may have also encountered intermittent issues setting custom statuses.We identified that a recent code change had resulted in localized emoji names being returned to our systems in error, which was causing status updates to fail.We deployed a fix in version 25.02.30, which should be available to all users via the Apple App Store shortly.
articles.title: Incident: Non-English iOS users can't set default status

articles.description: From around 5:00 PM PST on February 11, 2025 until around 1:00 PM PST on February 17, 2025, some users were unable to add existing workspace members to channels using their email addresses in bulk. Affected users reported the issue presenting as an endless loading icon or various errors appearing when entering user emails. It was also noted that some users were not displayed as existing members of the channel.We traced this issue back to a logic condition that would prevent Slack from returning proper results if there were multiple users with matching search query conditions. We removed the problematic condition within the code, resolving the issue for all affected users.
articles.title: Incident: Some users may have trouble adding multiple existing workspace members to channels by email address
